title: gRPC & Protocol Buffers
description: Production gRPC and Protocol Buffers reference covering messages, field presence, enums, oneofs, services, unary and streaming RPCs, deadlines, cancellation, metadata, status, retries, schema evolution, security, load balancing, health, reflection, testing, observability, and operations.

subtopics.title: Messages, Fields & Tag Numbers
subtopics.description: Messages define typed fields identified on the wire by stable numeric tags. Names can change more safely than numbers; numbers must never be reused for a different meaning.

callouts.title: Reserve Removed Tags and Names
callouts.text: Old serialized data and clients may still use them. Reusing a tag can reinterpret bytes as an unrelated field and silently corrupt meaning.

subtopics.title: Field Presence, Enums & oneof
subtopics.description: Presence distinguishes unset from a default-valued field where supported. Enums need an explicit zero unspecified value; oneof models mutually exclusive alternatives.

callouts.title: Unknown Enum Values Must Survive
callouts.text: New producers may send values older consumers do not recognize. Avoid exhaustive logic that crashes or silently maps unknown values to a business state.

subtopics.title: Repeated Fields, Maps & Well-Known Types
subtopics.description: Repeated fields preserve sequence, maps encode key/value entries without order guarantees, and well-known types standardize timestamps, durations, masks, emptiness, and dynamic values.

callouts.title: Avoid Struct and Any as Schema Escape Hatches
callouts.text: Dynamic containers weaken compatibility, validation, discoverability, and generated APIs. Use them only where genuinely open content is part of the contract.

subtopics.title: Unary, Server, Client & Bidirectional Streaming
subtopics.description: Service methods define request and response message types. Streaming changes backpressure, ordering, lifetime, load balancing, retries, and resource ownership.

subtopics.title: Deadlines, Cancellation & Flow Control
subtopics.description: Clients should set deadlines; servers propagate remaining budget downstream and stop unnecessary work when contexts cancel. Streaming APIs must respect transport flow control and application queue limits.

codeBlocks.code:
Caller deadline → propagated timeout/deadline metadata → server context
Server work → database/RPC calls use remaining budget
Cancellation → stop reads/writes, release resources, roll back/finish owned effects
Stream → bounded producer, await send readiness, no unbounded buffering

callouts.title: No Deadline Can Mean Forever
callouts.text: Library defaults vary. Define per-operation budgets, distinguish cancellation from deadline expiry, and ensure retries fit inside the original overall deadline.

subtopics.title: Metadata, Status Codes & Error Details
subtopics.description: Metadata carries transport-level context such as authorization and tracing; canonical status codes classify RPC outcomes. Structured error details convey safe machine-readable information.

codeBlocks.code:
INVALID_ARGUMENT → malformed/domain-invalid request
NOT_FOUND → requested resource absent for caller semantics
ALREADY_EXISTS / ABORTED → conflict or concurrency outcome
FAILED_PRECONDITION → state prevents operation
UNAUTHENTICATED → identity missing/invalid
PERMISSION_DENIED → caller authenticated but forbidden
UNAVAILABLE → transient service unavailability

callouts.title: Do Not Leak Internals in Status Messages
callouts.text: Map exceptions centrally, log full cause with correlation, and return stable codes/details without SQL, stack traces, filesystem paths, tokens, or private resource existence.

subtopics.title: Retries, Idempotency & Hedging
subtopics.description: Retry only classified transient failures and idempotent operations within a budget. Hedging sends another attempt before failure and can amplify load and duplicate effects.

codeBlocks.code:
Retry condition: method policy + status + idempotency + remaining deadline
Backoff: exponential + jitter + max attempts
Mutation: request ID / idempotency key stored with canonical result
Hedge: safe read only, bounded, cancel loser, capacity-tested

callouts.title: Never Retry Every UNAVAILABLE Blindly
callouts.text: Outages, overload, draining, and network failures can trigger retry storms. Coordinate client, proxy, service-mesh, and server retry ownership.

subtopics.title: Binary Wire, ProtoJSON & Compatibility
subtopics.description: Binary protobuf preserves unknown fields in supported runtimes and identifies fields by number. ProtoJSON uses names and has different compatibility limits; it does not carry unknown fields equivalently.

rows: Old peers ignore; define default behavior

callouts.title: Compatibility Is More Than Parsing
callouts.text: Units, validation, default meaning, authorization, ordering, and side effects can break even when bytes parse. Test cross-version behavior and retained historical data.

subtopics.title: Editions, Code Generation & Governance
subtopics.description: Protobuf Editions evolve language defaults independently of runtime package versions. Pin protoc, plugins, runtimes, edition, generated-code policy, and lint/breaking-change checks.

codeBlocks.code:
protoc --version
# Generate deterministically through pinned toolchain/container
# lint proto sources
# compare schema against main/released baseline
# regenerate all supported languages and run compatibility tests

callouts.title: Generated Code and Runtime Versions Must Be Compatible
callouts.text: Language runtimes have cross-version guarantees and limits. Upgrade compiler, plugins, generated code, and runtime according to official support policy rather than independently guessing.

subtopics.title: TLS, Authentication, Authorization & Interceptors
subtopics.description: Use TLS or mutual TLS, attach scoped credentials through metadata, validate identity at the server, authorize each method/resource, and use interceptors for cross-cutting policy with care.

codeBlocks.code:
Transport: TLS + verified server name; mTLS when workload identity requires it
Authentication: token/certificate → validated principal
Authorization: service/method + object + tenant + current policy
Interceptors: tracing, authn, policy, metrics, safe logging, deadline defaults
Never log authorization metadata or message secrets

callouts.title: Reflection Is an Operational Choice
callouts.text: Protect or disable it according to environment and tooling needs, but do not mistake obscurity for authorization. Every callable method remains secured.

subtopics.title: Health, Reflection, Name Resolution & Load Balancing
subtopics.description: Standard health services expose serving state; reflection enables dynamic tooling; client-side balancing depends on resolver/service config and connection behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
Resolver → endpoint addresses + service config
Channel/subchannels → connections and connectivity state
Policy → pick_first / round_robin / platform-specific balancing
Health → service-specific readiness, watch where supported
Shutdown → reject new work, drain streams, finish within deadline

callouts.title: One Long-Lived HTTP/2 Connection Can Pin Traffic
callouts.text: Understand whether balancing occurs at client, proxy, or connection level. Test endpoint changes, draining, keepalive, max connection age, and stream longevity.

subtopics.title: Testing, Observability & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Test generated contracts across languages, in-process/local behavior, real transport, deadlines, cancellation, streaming, compatibility, auth, and failure injection.

codeBlocks.code:
Metrics: calls started/completed, status, latency, message bytes, active streams
Traces: client/server spans with propagated context and RPC semantic attributes
Logs: method, safe principal/resource identifiers, status, request/trace ID
Tests: golden binary/JSON cases, old/new peer matrix, malformed/oversized inputs

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Reserve field tags, model presence, govern schemas, set deadlines, propagate cancellation, bound streams/messages, retry only idempotently, secure metadata and methods, configure health/balancing, observe status/latency, and test cross-version rollout and shutdown.
